Day 1: West Lake — a scenic freshwater lake surrounded by temples, pagodas, and gardens. Ideal for a relaxed family walk. Kids enjoy the boat rides and the musical fountain show at night.
[2] source=hangzhou.md; destination=Hangzhou; section=itinerary; score=0.89
Day 2: Lingyin Temple — one of China's largest and wealthiest Buddhist temples. The Fei Lai Feng grottoes feature hundreds of stone carvings. Children-friendly with wide paths and shaded areas.
[3] source=hangzhou.md; destination=Hangzhou; section=crowd_risk; score=0.85
Lingyin Temple can be very crowded on weekends. Best to visit on weekday mornings. West Lake is spacious enough to absorb crowds well.

Forbidden City — the largest imperial palace complex in the world. Budget tip: book tickets online in advance (60 RMB), avoid guide fees by using free audio apps. Allow 3-4 hours minimum.
[2] source=beijing.md; destination=Beijing; section=itinerary; score=0.91
Jingshan Park — directly north of Forbidden City. Entry only 2 RMB. Climb to the top pavilion for the best panoramic view of the palace rooftops and central Beijing skyline.
[3] source=beijing.md; destination=Beijing; section=crowd_risk; score=0.87
Forbidden City requires advance online reservation. Weekends sell out days ahead. Jingshan Park is less crowded. Subway Line 1 is the cheapest way to reach both sites (3-6 RMB per ride).

evidence:
[1] source=chengdu.md; destination=Chengdu; section=itinerary; score=0.93
Jinli Ancient Street — a restored Qing dynasty street with traditional snacks, crafts, and tea houses. Great for solo travelers: sample mapo tofu, dan dan noodles, and Sichuan hot pot at small stalls.
[2] source=chengdu.md; destination=Chengdu; section=itinerary; score=0.90
Wuhou Shrine — memorial temple dedicated to Zhuge Liang. Peaceful gardens and historical exhibits. Budget-friendly entry (60 RMB). Combine with Jinli visit (adjacent).
[3] source=chengdu.md; destination=Chengdu; section=crowd_risk; score=0.84
Jinli can be extremely crowded during holidays and weekends. Visit on weekday evenings for a more relaxed street food experience. Wuhou Shrine is generally uncrowded.
